title: CYBERDOOM — Retro 3D First-Person Shooter Studio
description: A complete, production-ready, 100% client-side retro 3D first-person shooter built with vanilla HTML5, CSS3, ES6 and Three.js r128. Three procedurally generated sectors, billboard enemies, hitscan weapons, Web Audio synthesis, Doom-style HUD, localStorage autosave and JSON save transfer.

tokens.note: Snapshot from the OpenCode session record when the project was packaged. total = input + output + reasoning. Cache reads/writes are context-usage figures and are listed separately. The final state commit, GitHub push and Pages verification happen after this snapshot, so the live session totals are marginally higher.

cost.note: As reported by the OpenCode session record.

game.render: low-resolution WebGL canvas scaled with image-rendering: pixelated + CRT/scanline overlays
game.levelGeneration: seeded recursive-backtracker maze, carved rooms, braided loops, BFS reachability, far-room exit placement, A* enemy navigation
features: PointerLockControls FPS movement with sprint, jump and collision
procedural wall/floor/ceiling textures, props, signage and ceiling lights
enemy state machine with patrol, alert, chase and attack
hitscan ray verification, headshots, spread, range falloff
particle hit sparks, tracers, muzzle-flash point light and screen shake
procedural plasma gun / super shotgun viewmodels with recoil and sway
Doom-style status bar and animated marine portrait
minimap, compass, objective tracker and message feed
procedural Web Audio SFX and ambient drone
localStorage autosave, JSON export/import, high-score archive

verification.browser: Headless Chrome 156 (WebGL via ANGLE/Metal) and SwiftShader fallback
checks: dungeon connectivity, start/exit reachability and pathfinding
plasma and shotgun hitscan damage and kill scoring
enemy AI aggro, chase and projectile damage
health, armour absorption and face-state changes
pause/resume, save download and real file-input import
exit unlock, Space interaction, three-sector progression and victory
high-score recording and persistence across reload
zero uncaught exceptions and zero console errors

performance.note: Observed in the headless Chrome test environment; the renderer caps internal resolution and can be tuned from the pause menu.
